et tidspunkt.explanation: "Et tidspunkt" means "a point in time". To say "at that time", use "på det tidspunkt" (at that time): "På det tidspunkt var jeg hjemme" (At that time I was at home).

et tidsrum.explanation: "Et tidsrum" means "a period of time". To say between which times, use "i tidsrummet mellem" (in the period between): "i tidsrummet mellem otte og ti" (in the period between eight and ten). For one exact moment, use "et tidspunkt" (a point in time): "Hvilket tidspunkt passer dig?" (Which time suits you?)

et tilbageslag.explanation: "Et tilbageslag" means "a setback". It is built from "tilbage" (back) and "et slag" (a blow). To say you suffer one, use "at få" (to get): "Han fik et tilbageslag i sin bedring" (He suffered a setback in his recovery).

et tilbud.explanation: "Et tilbud" means "an offer / deal". To say a shop sells something cheaper for a while, use "på tilbud" (on sale): "Kaffen er på tilbud" (The coffee is on sale).

et tilbudskatalog.explanation: "Et tilbudskatalog" means "a sale catalog". It is built from "et tilbud" (an offer) and "et katalog" (a catalog).

et tilfælde.explanation: "Et tilfælde" means "a case / coincidence". To say something happened by chance, use "ved et tilfælde" (by chance): "Jeg mødte hende ved et tilfælde" (I met her by chance). For a case in court, use "en sag" (a case): "Sagen kommer for retten i morgen" (The case goes to court tomorrow).

et tilholdssted.explanation: "Et tilholdssted" means "a hangout / haunt". It is built from "at holde til" (to stay somewhere regularly) and "et sted" (a place).

et tillægsord.explanation: "Et tillægsord" means "an adjective". It is built from "et tillæg" (an addition) and "et ord" (a word). Another word for it is "et adjektiv" (an adjective).

et tiltag.explanation: "Et tiltag" means "an initiative / measure". To say what a step is aimed at, add "mod" (against): "nye tiltag mod trafikstøj" (new measures against traffic noise).

et tip.explanation: "Et tip" means "a tip", as in a helpful suggestion. To say you leave money for service, use "drikkepenge" (tip money): "Vi gav tjeneren drikkepenge" (We gave the waiter a tip).

et tog.explanation: "Et tog" means "a train". To say you travel by train, use "med toget" (by train): "Jeg rejser med toget" (I travel by train). The same spelling is also the past tense of "at tage" (to take): "Han tog min bog" (He took my book).

et toilet.explanation: "Et toilet" means "a toilet". To ask where the restroom is, say "Hvor er toilettet?" (Where is the toilet?)

et topmøde.explanation: "Et topmøde" means "a summit". It is built from "en top" (a top) and "et møde" (a meeting).

et tordenvejr.explanation: "Et tordenvejr" means "a thunderstorm". It is built from "torden" (thunder) and "vejr" (weather), the same "vejr" as in "regnvejr" (rainy weather) and "solskinsvejr" (sunny weather).

et torv.explanation: "Et torv" means "a square", as in an open space in a town. Copenhagen has a square named "Gammeltorv" (Old Square).

et trafiklys.explanation: "Et trafiklys" means "a traffic light". It is built from "trafik" (traffic) and "et lys" (a light). When you mean a candle, "et lys" works too: "et lys på bordet" (a candle on the table).

et trick.explanation: "Et trick" means "a trick". To say you do a trick, use "at lave" (to do, to make): "Han laver et trick med en mønt" (He does a trick with a coin).

et trin.explanation: "Et trin" means "a step", as in one stair of a staircase or one stage in a process. For a step you take with your foot, use "et skridt" (a step): "Tag et skridt frem" (Take a step forward).

et tryk.explanation: "Et tryk" means "a pressure / stress". To say you press a button, use "et tryk på knappen" (a press on the button). In "blodtryk" (blood pressure), "tryk" means "pressure".

et træ.explanation: "Et træ" means "a tree". To say what something is made of, use "træ" (wood) after "af" (of): "et bord af træ" (a table made of wood). For a large group of trees, use "en skov" (a forest): "Vi går en tur i skoven" (We go for a walk in the forest).

et træk.explanation: "Et træk" means "a move". To praise a clever move, say "Det var et smart træk" (That was a smart move). To say cold air blows through a room, use "træk" (a draft): "Der er træk i stuen" (There is a draft in the room).

et træningspas.explanation: "Et træningspas" means "a training session". To talk about exercising in general, use "træning" (training): "Træning er sundt" (Exercise is healthy).

et tv.explanation: "Et tv" means "a TV". To say you watch TV, use "at se tv" (literally, "to see TV").

et tv-program.explanation: "Et tv-program" means "a TV program". For a show with many episodes, use "en tv-serie" (a TV series): "Jeg ser en tv-serie om en detektiv" (I watch a TV series about a detective).

et tyveri.explanation: "Et tyveri" means "a theft". It comes from "en tyv" (a thief). To say you report a theft, use "at anmelde" (to report): "Jeg vil gerne anmelde et tyveri" (I would like to report a theft).
